To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified loci and genes associated with important agronomical traits in rice varieties adapted to temperates regions.
we have identified loci controlling important agronomic trait among rice cultivars adapted to the temperate conditions.

we have identified a set of markers that can be used for the genetic improvement in rice cultivars grown in temperate conditions, and that some of them have been associated with genes that have not been previously linked to the traits studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new markers for the genetic improvement in the rice breeding programs.
the identification of molecular markers associated with important agronomical traits in a panel of japonica rice varieties adapted to temperates regions.
the study of the genetic bases of adaptation of rice cultivars to temperate climates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has provided a set of markers that can help to elucidate and understand the genetic mechanism underlying the regulation of the different traits, and also to improve the agronomical traits of japonica cultivars grown in temperate regions.
the present results represent an important contribution towards the identification of the genetic bases of the adaptation of rice to the environment in temperate regions.
the association study performed in this work has provided new molecular markers associated with important agronomical traits in rice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a set of SNPs associated with important agronomical traits in rice varieties cultivated in temperate conditions.
we have identified a set of molecular markers associated to important traits for rice breeding, which can be useful for marker-assisted selection.
the association mapping approach can be a useful and efficient tool to detect genetic markers associated with agronomically important traits in temperate japonica varieties.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to identify molecular markers associated with agronomic traits in a panel of rice varieties that are not inbred lines, but instead are elite varieties that are widely used by farmers in the field.
association studies in rice can provide new insights into the genetic basis of complex traits, even in the case of populations adapted to specific environments.

the use of a panel of rice varieties adapted to specific agro-climate condition can provide a useful resource for the identification of molecular markers that can contribute to the breeding programs in the corresponding regions.
